findings.body:
**Reject all state events during prepare-only inventory.**

Line [97] rejects only events for the retired job. If preparation emits `inventory enqueue` for a new job, the assertion still passes. Use `event.assert_not_called()` to cover both event paths. The operator must validate the snapshot before it emits either event.
findings.title: Reject all state events during prepare-only inventory.

findings.body:
**Observe lock contention before releasing the first collector.**

Line [342] signals `attempted` before the second worker attempts to acquire the lock. If that worker pauses until the first collector finishes, a broken implementation that uses separate locks for the two output paths can pass the timeout, snapshot order, and final catalog checks. Signal from a contention probe that confirms the second worker cannot acquire its output lock while the first holds it. Keep the independent output as a control.
findings.title: Observe lock contention before releasing the first collector.

findings.body:
**Test the wrong digest without a live owner.**

At Line [295], both digest cases use an item with a nonempty `run`. If `release` ignores the digest but still rejects live owners, both calls raise `IntegrityError` and the test passes. Use an unowned blocked item for the wrong digest. Keep the live-owner case with an exact digest.
findings.title: Test the wrong digest without a live owner.

findings.body:
**Check that the busy-lock response is one JSON artifact.**

Line [151] accepts plain text or extra output as long as stdout contains `queue lock busy`. Parse the entire captured stdout as JSON, then check the diagnostic in that value. Keep the exit-code assertion. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Check that the busy-lock response is one JSON artifact.

findings.body:
**Include file modes in the read-only artifact check.**

If a render changes the mode of `dist/queue-runner/crq.js` without changing its bytes, this assertion still passes. The artifact is outside the checkout, so the Git status assertion cannot detect the change. Record each entry’s type and mode with `lstat()` in both snapshots. Use the same snapshot helper for the check at Line 379.
findings.title: Include file modes in the read-only artifact check.

findings.body:
**Reject commands that can start units during prepare.**

`systemctl --user restart crq-tick.service` can start the inactive service, but neither token checked here is present. The fixture records the command and returns success, so the test still passes. Assert that `daemon-reload` is the only mutating `systemctl` operation. Keep the read-only probes allowed.
findings.title: Reject commands that can start units during prepare.

findings.body:
**Assert that a digest mismatch prevents helper import.**

If the controller imports `prepare-host.py` and then rejects its digest before lock or preflight, every assertion in this test still passes. The invalid `--sha` checks refusal order relative to preflight, not import. Observe whether the helper loader runs and require zero calls on a mismatch. Keep the matching-digest test as the success control.
findings.title: Assert that a digest mismatch prevents helper import.

findings.body:
**Check the deployment phase as well as the compatibility SHA.**

Three calls with `self.prior` before the switch satisfy both assertions, even if the driver never checks compatibility after the switch. Record each call’s phase using the drain and switch boundaries. Require a check before hold, after drain, and after switch, with `self.prior` in each phase.
findings.title: Check the deployment phase as well as the compatibility SHA.

findings.body:
**Move the queue change into the health callback in the rollback-disabled health test.**

The test named for a failed health check never calls the health callback. Its queue write runs inside the switch wrapper. The deploy driver checks queue bytes after the switch and before the health window. That check raises first, so the run fails on the byte-preservation check. The `"automatic rollback is disabled"` assertion matches a later refusal from the rollback path.

Write the schema-marked queue inside the health callback instead. The byte check then passes. The health result fails, and the rollback refusal is reached through the health path.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
     def test_health_failure_keeps_hold_when_rollback_is_disabled(self):
-        real_switch = host.switch
-
-        def dirtying_switch(root, overlay, raw, target, tag=None):
-            result = real_switch(root, overlay, raw, target, tag)
-            (self.runner / "state/queue.json").write_text(
-                '{"schema_version": 3, "items": []}\n')
-            return result
+        def unhealthy_after_queue_change():
+            (self.runner / "state/queue.json").write_text(
+                '{"schema_version": 3, "items": []}\n')
+            return {"healthy": False, "reason": "no advancing tick"}

         helper = mock.Mock(wraps=None)
         helper.load_overlay = host.load_overlay
         helper.root_check = host.root_check
         helper.verify_target = host.verify_target
-        helper.switch = dirtying_switch
-        run = self.build(helper=helper, health=lambda: {
-            "healthy": False, "reason": "no advancing tick"})
+        helper.switch = host.switch
+        run = self.build(helper=helper, health=unhealthy_after_queue_change)
```

</details>
findings.title: Move the queue change into the health callback in the rollback-disabled health test.

findings.body:
**Use an age well inside the 3600-second limit in the fresh-snapshot test.**

`backlog()` stamps the snapshot with the real clock at `test_repair_backlog.py:210`, and `stamp()` drops fractional seconds (`test_repair_backlog.py:22`). `hold_backfill_groups` reads the clock again at `crq_repair.py:1064` and admits the snapshot only when `0 <= age <= BACKLOG_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (`crq_repair.py:1065`, with the constant at `crq_repair.py:1030` set to 3600). With `age=3599`, the stored age is 3599 plus the truncated fraction plus any elapsed time before admission. If the fraction and the delay together reach one second, the snapshot is stale. Only `pr-review` is kept, and the assertion at line 259 fails. This can happen intermittently under scheduler load.

Use an age that leaves a wide margin:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-        self.backlog(0, 36, age=3599)
+        self.backlog(0, 36, age=60)
```

</details>
findings.title: Use an age well inside the 3600-second limit in the fresh-snapshot test.
